title: Proposed CoSAI SRF next-version agentic extensions
status: Independently proposed companion extension of the CoSAI Shared Responsibility Framework; not part of CoSAI SRF v1.0; not endorsed by CoSAI or OASIS.
description: Nine asks for a future CoSAI SRF revision. Each record names the v1.0 hook it extends, the site surfaces that already use it, and what the next paper should add. These are companion ideas on this site, not a competing framework.

refused.label: AI SAFE² ACT-1 to ACT-4
refused.reason: Same collision. At most a crosswalk footnote, never a live scale.

refused.label: AISM Chaos-to-Sovereignty
refused.reason: Competing maturity architecture; not an SRF noun.

refused.label: HEAR doctrine
refused.reason: Keep fail-closed named halt authority; do not add a ninth persona or a branded named-key ritual.

refused.label: Control Envelope as an SRF object
refused.reason: Control already means an accountability assignment with ID, layer, persona, operating models, and threshold.

items.title: Accountability continuity
items.v1_0_hook: Section 3, exactly one accountable party per activity; CoSAI IAM non-expanding delegation
items.cosai_vnext_ask: State that delegated authority must not silently expand, and that a child agent's authority stays inside the parent assignment. Keep the one-party rule; add continuity across delegation hops.

items.title: Spawn and replication as a named activity
items.v1_0_hook: L3 / Agent-PaaS matrices; agent definitions on a provider runtime
items.cosai_vnext_ask: Add spawn authority, descendant capability narrowing, live descendant inventory, and revocation of the full descendant tree as a named Agent-PaaS / L3 activity.

items.title: Fail-closed halt when the authorizer is unreachable
items.v1_0_hook: Appendix A.1.3.2, Human Override Tiers T1-T5
items.cosai_vnext_ask: For irreversible, financially material, security-control-modifying, physical, or cross-organization actions, block if the assigned override authority cannot be reached. Do not import a named-individual brand.

items.title: Persistence scope on L2
items.v1_0_hook: L2 AI Information, retention and access prose
items.cosai_vnext_ask: Classify information effects as request, handle_scoped, or durable, and name the accountable persona for durable state.

items.title: Enforcement-plane declaration
items.v1_0_hook: Operating-model matrices; Appendix A.1.3 agentic attributes
items.cosai_vnext_ask: Treat north-south, east-west, and agent-to-tool as an attribute on agentic deployments, like autonomy_scope. Not a sixth architecture layer. Name which persona owns each plane under each operating model.

items.title: Protocol-independent evidence
items.cosai_vnext_ask: Bind evidence to principals, capability grants, delegation chains, policy versions, and state handles, not to a session identifier owned by a protocol.

items.title: Owner coverage vs halt-authority coverage
items.v1_0_hook: Section 3 personas; Appendix A.1.3.2 override tiers
items.cosai_vnext_ask: Require that halt authority is assigned and measurable, and that persona assignment and halt-authority coverage can be audited separately. Do not add a ninth persona.
inspired_by: AI SAFE² owner_of_record vs halt authority

items.title: Spend ceiling as a halt, not only an alert
items.v1_0_hook: L3 application safety; L4 platform; Agent-PaaS
items.cosai_vnext_ask: Name spend or economic ceiling as an Agent-PaaS / L3-L4 control with halt vs alert semantics and one accountable persona.

items.title: Control-plane location per operating model
items.cosai_vnext_ask: Each matrix should state where authorization is enforced (customer app, Agent-PaaS runtime, model-provider gateway), distinct from where the agent executes.
